### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every case ran one fixed sequence: A21 was always followed by A22 (100% of A21's outgoing transitions), A22 was always followed by A23, and A23 always sat exactly two positions after A21. The activities A27, A28 and A33 were not observed in any of the 200 earlier traces. [DIR001, REL001, REL005, LAG001, REL012]
- In the later window, about half of the cases (roughly 100 in 200) still run this original A21 → A22 → A23 sequence: A21 and A22 co-occur in 51% of traces, A22 and A23 in 51%, and A23 is two positions after A21 in 51%. [REL001, REL005, LAG001]
- In the remaining 98 of 200 later cases, A22 is skipped and a block of three activities — A27, A28 and A33 — runs between A21 and A23. A21's outgoing transitions now lead to A22 in about 51% of cases and to A28 (about 18%), A33 (about 17%) and A27 (about 15%) in the rest. [DIR001, REL001]
- The three block activities always occur together: each appears in 98 of 200 traces, each pair of them co-occurs in the same 49% of traces, and none of them ever co-occurs with A22 — A22 and the block behave as strict alternatives. Within the block there is no fixed order (for A27 and A28, both orders occur in about 23 and 27 of 100 traces), and each member is sometimes the one followed by A23 (about 30% of A27's outgoing transitions, 27% of A28's, 44% of A33's). [POS001, POS002, POS003, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL012, REL013, REL014, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- The block sits around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.49 for all three activities, unobserved before), always after A21 and before A23: each of A27, A28 and A33 co-occurs with A21 in 49% of traces with A21 first, and precedes A23 in the same 49%. [POS001, POS002, POS003, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL009, REL010, REL011]
- Consistently, the distance from A21 to A23 doubles in exactly these cases: A23 lies four positions after A21 in 49% of later traces, versus always two positions in the earlier window. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural change in the later window: in about half of the cases (98 of 200), a new route between A21 and A23 is taken in which the block A27–A28–A33 — all three executed together, in no fixed internal order — replaces A22, while the original A21 → A22 → A23 sequence continues in the other half. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL001, REL005, REL006, REL009, LAG001]

The hypothesis is supported directly and consistently: successor evidence shows A21 gaining edges to the block and the block gaining edges to each other and to A23, none of which were observed earlier; relational evidence shows A22 and each block member as mutually exclusive while each block member sits between A21 and A23; positional evidence shows the block appearing mid-trace where it was previously absent; and the A21-to-A23 distance doubles from two to four positions in exactly the new-variant traces. All 22 flagged items describe this one coherent structure, and the screening flagged 22 control-flow items where fewer than one (0.24) would be expected by chance, so the set as a whole cannot be explained by random re-splitting of the two windows. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, LAG001]

Limitations: the evidence is entirely control-flow and cannot show whether the block's mixed internal order reflects an unordered sequence or parallel execution, nor why cases take one route or the other. An important competing explanation it cannot fully rule out is that A27, A28 and A33 existed earlier but were too rare to be sampled — zero participation in the earlier window only means "not observed" — although a behaviour present in 98 of 200 later traces being missed across 200 earlier traces makes this unlikely. [POS001, POS002, POS003, REL012, REL013, REL014]
